note: The same byte through the WRITER, which is where the two sides part. Emacs prints "a\342b" -- it escapes a byte that is not a character back into the octal form that reads again. kg prints the raw 0xE2 verbatim, so its own output is not valid UTF-8 and does not read back as the string it came from. Recorded before Phase 25.1 touches the writer, because `%S`'s job is to produce something the reader accepts.
